items.summary: a16z 发布对 100 名千人员以上企业 CISO 的调研，87% 预期 2027 年安全支出增长，主要受 AI 威胁和自身 AI 部署扩大攻击面驱动。2027 年最受关注的七项安全举措全部与 AI 相关，其中 SOC 自动化获最多首选票，内部 AI agent 安全、SOC 自动化和进攻性安全升幅最大，但 AI SOC 工具生产环境使用率仅 18%。

en.summary: a16z surveyed 100 CISOs at companies with more than 1,000 employees: 87% expect security spending to rise by 2027, driven mainly by AI threats and the expanded attack surface from their own AI deployments. en.title: AI-Native Organization Implementation Handbook: Illustrated Edition
en.summary: This illustrated handbook for putting an AI-native organization into practice breaks community collaboration into a workable closed loop: first spell out the task, ownership, document version, and authorization boundaries; have AI deliver a small sample first, flagging its sources and gaps; then, after human review, execute, log the results, and update through retrospective. If you're also looking to bring AI into your team's day-to-day operations, it's worth a close read.
en.reason: An illustrated AI-native organization manual turns event preparation into a closed loop: define service targets, deliverables, deadlines and authorization boundaries, assign drafting/checking/execution/material-maintenance roles, then require AI to submit small samples with evidence and gaps before human review and updates.

en.title: After hundreds of rounds of daily conversations with AI, I started looking into how to worry less
en.summary: The author shares lessons from long-term human-AI collaboration, building workflows with the Cohub visual workbench and the Mirasim multi-person + AI collaborative space. The piece also explores often-overlooked pain points such as asynchronous collaboration between people and AI, permission maintenance, and trust building. This human-centered, symbiotic approach is well worth a look for anyone using AI intensively for creative development.

en.title: From a 3-Day Demo to Company-Wide Adoption in a Month: How Xiaohongshu Scaled Its Enterprise AI Assistant Seal
en.summary:
Word count: 7,802 words
Reading time: about 26 minutes

Xiaohongshu built the beta version of its AI assistant Seal on OpenClaw in three days and rolled it out company-wide within a month, focusing on rapid validation and scaled deployment under the premise of security and controllability.

Key points: opting for secondary development on open source rather than building in-house, balancing speed and controllability; making security a hard architectural constraint up front rather than bolting it on afterward; using modular design to achieve memory, capability reuse, and ecosystem expansion.

Intended for AI platform engineers, enterprise Agent architects, and technical decision-makers.

At the AICon Global AI Development and Application Conference, Xiaohongshu architect Meng Hongjin shared the company's experience building Seal, an enterprise-grade AI personal assistant. Before the Spring Festival, the Xiaohongshu team launched an internal beta based on OpenClaw and shipped the first version in just three days; after validating the product's value, it quickly completed an architecture upgrade and scaled the rollout, achieving company-wide coverage within a month.

Going from a demo to tens of thousands of users isn't just about deploying an Agent. Enterprises must also solve a range of problems including security, cost, memory, capability reuse, and product ecosystem. Drawing on the full build-out of Seal, this article explains how Xiaohongshu tackled these challenges and how the team thinks about the next generation of agents.

en.reason: Xiaohongshu architect Meng Hongjin recounts building Seal on OpenClaw in three days, filling 2,000 beta spots in five minutes, reaching full company coverage in a month, and detailing cluster-, runtime- and data-layer security and cost governance.

items.recommend_reason_zh: 10月22日，InfoQ AI侦察团@QCon上海2026首次集结，带成员听阿里巴巴等主论坛分享，并在阿里云、亚马逊云科技等四场实战专场中拆解企业AI落地。
items.summary:
本文字数：2322 字
阅读完需：约 8 分钟
10 月 22 日，由 InfoQ 极客传媒主办，联合中欧国际工商学院 EMBA 课程部、独角兽创业营、TGO 鲲鹏会共同发起的 InfoQ AI 侦察团 @QCon 上海 2026 首次集结。
从 QCon 上海主论坛，到午餐圆桌、技术专场和闭门私董会，成员们在一天中听技术、聊实践、谈问题，也尝试从其他同侪的经验中寻找企业 AI 落地的解决思路。

en.title: AWS open-sources Agent "Decider" and "Safety Box," but concurrency and cold starts remain unresolved
en.summary:
AWS launches Strands Decider 2B and Strands Box to boost AI agent development.
Word count: 1,591; reading time: about 5 minutes.
AWS has open-sourced Strands Decider 2B (a 2-billion-parameter decision model) and Strands Box (an execution sandbox), addressing lightweight decision-making and secure execution in agent workflows. Decider 2B uses a pointer head plus LoRA fine-tuning and focuses on multi-option scoring and routing. It achieves latency in the 100ms range on consumer-grade hardware and 72.3% accuracy on JevBench.
It supports model routing and tool selection; provides deterministic decisions with confidence scores; and offers out-of-the-box CLI and Strands agent integration.
Intended for AI engineers, agent architects, and MLOps engineers.

en.reason: AWS open-sourced the 2-billion-parameter Strands Decider 2B decision model and Strands Box execution sandbox, with the model hitting 72.3% on JevBench at roughly 115ms latency while concurrency and cold-start delays remain unresolved.

en.title:
Chinese AI Models Go Global as Regulatory Boundaries Come Into Focus

Chinese AI companies are asking whether training or running advanced models on overseas servers owned by foreign companies would trigger technology export rules, according to an October 28 Reuters report shared by Bill Bishop.
en.reason: China's Commerce Ministry is consulting on a catalogue revision published October 16 that would add 23 AI technologies, including large models and agents, to export controls with temporary registration already in force, while clarifying that API, App and SaaS calls from abroad do not count as technology exports but leaving the status of foreign-owned overseas servers unresolved.

en.title:
Douyin penalizes 507,000 accounts, calls out AI marketing accounts ⚠️

Douyin recently issued a governance notice aimed squarely at marketing accounts that use AI to mass-produce accounts, and one number stands out:

507,000 violating accounts penalized in the past month.

That's right — over the same period it also took down 1.135 million violating videos. Specifically called out: AI digital humans impersonating celebrities' relatives to sell products, AI mimicking celebrity voices to mass-produce quote videos, and mass copying of viral templates.
en.reason: Douyin’s latest governance notice reports 507,000 violating accounts and 1.135 million violating videos removed in about a month, naming AI digital personas impersonating celebrities’ relatives to sell goods, AI-cloned celebrity voices generating quote content, and bulk copying of viral templates, while stressing that AI-assisted writing or editing is not itself targeted—only malicious marketing accounts using AI as a shortcut to traffic monetization.

en.title: Long read: why is today's local AI just a toy for enthusiasts?
en.reason: Veteran AI blogger Matthew Berman argues that locally running AI, which means fully offline execution on your own hardware rather than cloud-hosted open-source models, makes little practical sense for most people because cost and experience are wildly disproportionate.

items.title: 当AI智能体开始24小时炒币，真正赚钱的究竟是AI，还是交易所？ 我最近一直在思考一个问题。 假设未来有100万个AI智能体同时进入加密货币市场，会发生什么？ 它们不需要睡觉。 可以24小时监控比特币价格、研究订单簿、分析新闻、追踪链上资金流，甚至观察其他AI正在买入什么。 有的AI负责追涨。 有的负责套利。 有的专门预测短期价格变化。 还有的模仿那些看起来最成功的交易者。 听起来，整个市场都会变得异常聪明。 但我突然意识到一件事。…

en.title: When AI agents start trading crypto 24/7, who's really making money—the AI or the exchange?
en.reason: A hypothetical 1 million AI agents trading crypto 24/7 — monitoring Bitcoin prices, order books, news and on-chain flows as momentum chasers, arbitrageurs, short-term forecasters and copycats — raises the question of whether exchanges, not the AI, earn regardless of trading profits.

en.title: Are world models the endgame for AI?
en.summary:
Are world models the endgame of AI?

Google has just released Genie 4, its next-generation world model. It generates a virtual world in real time — you can step inside, explore freely and change the environment, and the whole world shifts in response to what you do.

Some people are already asking whether open-world games like GTA could one day be generated directly by AI.

But others question whether these lifelike visuals are actually simulating real physics, or just a visual performance.

I think world models could be a key technology for AI's next stage, and could become the infrastructure for physical AI.

If this approach works, it could become an important foundation for AI moving from digital tasks to real-world action.

——

What exactly is a world model?

In the past, large language models mainly worked through text, images…
en.reason: Google's newly released Genie 4 world model generates a virtual world in real time that users can freely explore and alter, and the piece asks whether its realistic visuals actually simulate physical laws or are just a visual performance, and whether such models could become infrastructure for physical AI.

en.title: A recent long-form post by Anthropic platform lead Katelyn Lesse, titled "A New Set of Problems Software Engineers Need to Solve," has gone viral. It really resonated with me, so I wanted to share it with you all.
en.summary:
Anthropic platform lead Katelyn Lesse's long post, "A New Set of Problems Software Engineers Need to Solve," has gone viral, and it hit home for me — wanted to share it.

In it, she notes that many programmers are going through what amounts to an identity crisis, because the work itself has changed beyond recognition.

Some feel demoralized; others feel they're having the most fun of their lives.

Her take: over the next few years, software engineers will need to step up and solve a whole set of problems before AI can reach its real potential — and right now is a great time to be a software engineer.

Multi-agent systems are giving rise to a slew of new problems. Infrastructure has to evolve to handle more bursty workloads, agent authentication and authorization mechanisms need maturing, and better observability is needed so that when a system drifts off course…
en.reason: Anthropic platform lead Katelyn Lesse argues that multi-agent systems are forcing infrastructure to handle burstier workloads and demand better agent identity authentication, authorization and monitoring as AI scales.

en.title: In the past, I used to write from time to time — reflections, musings, everyday life, all sorts of things.
en.summary:
Once in a while I used to write something — reflections, random thoughts, bits of daily life, all sorts of things. Since AI came along, I've written less and less. I often get anxious about the things I post: is my language flowery enough, are there grammar mistakes in how I express myself, are the photos polished enough. Hand it to AI and a few sentences from me become a long piece far better than anything I'd write myself; worst case, I have it revise a few more times until I'm satisfied — after all, picking holes is easier than creating.

The first large model I tried was ERNIE Bot, one of the earliest generative language models, I suppose, though you hardly hear about it anymore. Then GPT-3.5 took off and I switched to GPT. Back then I had to get a friend overseas to help me pay for a membership, and I never once hit the cap on the $20 version — though it regularly got dumbed down, which was infuriating.

en.title:
Chinese AI Models Go Global as Regulatory Boundaries Come Into Focus

Chinese AI companies are asking whether training or running advanced models on overseas servers owned by foreign companies would trigger technology export rules, according to an October 28 Reuters report shared by Bill Bishop.
en.reason: China's Commerce Ministry is consulting on a catalogue revision published October 16 that would add 23 AI technologies, including large models and agents, to export controls with temporary registration already in force, while clarifying that API, App and SaaS calls from abroad do not count as technology exports but leaving the status of foreign-owned overseas servers unresolved.

en.title:
Douyin penalizes 507,000 accounts, calls out AI marketing accounts ⚠️

Douyin recently issued a governance notice aimed squarely at marketing accounts that use AI to mass-produce accounts, and one number stands out:

507,000 violating accounts penalized in the past month.

That's right — over the same period it also took down 1.135 million violating videos. Specifically called out: AI digital humans impersonating celebrities' relatives to sell products, AI mimicking celebrity voices to mass-produce quote videos, and mass copying of viral templates.
en.reason: Douyin’s latest governance notice reports 507,000 violating accounts and 1.135 million violating videos removed in about a month, naming AI digital personas impersonating celebrities’ relatives to sell goods, AI-cloned celebrity voices generating quote content, and bulk copying of viral templates, while stressing that AI-assisted writing or editing is not itself targeted—only malicious marketing accounts using AI as a shortcut to traffic monetization.

en.title: Are world models the endgame for AI?
en.summary:
Are world models the endgame of AI?

Google has just released Genie 4, its next-generation world model. It generates a virtual world in real time — you can step inside, explore freely and change the environment, and the whole world shifts in response to what you do.

Some people are already asking whether open-world games like GTA could one day be generated directly by AI.

But others question whether these lifelike visuals are actually simulating real physics, or just a visual performance.

I think world models could be a key technology for AI's next stage, and could become the infrastructure for physical AI.

If this approach works, it could become an important foundation for AI moving from digital tasks to real-world action.

——

What exactly is a world model?

In the past, large language models mainly worked through text, images…
en.reason: Google's newly released Genie 4 world model generates a virtual world in real time that users can freely explore and alter, and the piece asks whether its realistic visuals actually simulate physical laws or are just a visual performance, and whether such models could become infrastructure for physical AI.

en.title: A recent long-form post by Anthropic platform lead Katelyn Lesse, titled "A New Set of Problems Software Engineers Need to Solve," has gone viral. It really resonated with me, so I wanted to share it with you all.
en.summary:
Anthropic platform lead Katelyn Lesse's long post, "A New Set of Problems Software Engineers Need to Solve," has gone viral, and it hit home for me — wanted to share it.

In it, she notes that many programmers are going through what amounts to an identity crisis, because the work itself has changed beyond recognition.

Some feel demoralized; others feel they're having the most fun of their lives.

Her take: over the next few years, software engineers will need to step up and solve a whole set of problems before AI can reach its real potential — and right now is a great time to be a software engineer.

Multi-agent systems are giving rise to a slew of new problems. Infrastructure has to evolve to handle more bursty workloads, agent authentication and authorization mechanisms need maturing, and better observability is needed so that when a system drifts off course…
en.reason: Anthropic platform lead Katelyn Lesse argues that multi-agent systems are forcing infrastructure to handle burstier workloads and demand better agent identity authentication, authorization and monitoring as AI scales.

en.title: In the past, I used to write from time to time — reflections, musings, everyday life, all sorts of things.
en.summary:
Once in a while I used to write something — reflections, random thoughts, bits of daily life, all sorts of things. Since AI came along, I've written less and less. I often get anxious about the things I post: is my language flowery enough, are there grammar mistakes in how I express myself, are the photos polished enough. Hand it to AI and a few sentences from me become a long piece far better than anything I'd write myself; worst case, I have it revise a few more times until I'm satisfied — after all, picking holes is easier than creating.

The first large model I tried was ERNIE Bot, one of the earliest generative language models, I suppose, though you hardly hear about it anymore. Then GPT-3.5 took off and I switched to GPT. Back then I had to get a friend overseas to help me pay for a membership, and I never once hit the cap on the $20 version — though it regularly got dumbed down, which was infuriating.

The AI of that time — you could say that when it came to editing code, it was still far from…

First, the background: this is the largest upgrade to the evaluation system since v4 launched in January, raising the difficulty of the benchmarks while introducing a high share of private datasets and heavy agentic workflows.
en.summary:
AA's Index v5 has finally launched. Here’s a quick look at the key points:

1. Background: This is the largest overhaul of the evaluation system since v4 launched in January, raising difficulty and introducing a high proportion of private datasets and agent-heavy workflows.

2. v5 breaks model capabilities into four dimensions: knowledge work, coding, scientific research, and general capabilities and hallucination resistance, each weighted at 25%.

3. In the overall rankings, Opus 5.5 took first place with 58 points, followed by GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol. Anthropic and OpenAI swept the top five, with Google's Gemini 4 Argon behind them.

4. The gap between open-source and closed-source models has widened from 3 points to 12–26…

en.summary:
Finally found a way to let any Agent produce video results like Opus 5.5 with one click!! A one-stop solution covering the entire workflow from generation to editing and rendering!!

Many people want to use Opus 5.5 for motion graphics and editing, but have been held back by Claude subscription issues. After several days of research and testing, I've found an excellent alternative that lets you easily produce high-quality video with Codex or even domestic Agents like workbuddy.

At its core is Renoise MCP. Once connected to an Agent, it can automatically handle the entire workflow based on your ideas—from storyboard planning and video asset generation to editing, scoring, and final rendering.
